t: You're looking at 1 to 8 Collingham Gardens, a row of eight Grade II* listed houses in Kensington and Chelsea. They were built between 1883 and 1888 by the firm of Ernest George and Peto. Architecturally, they are regarded as representative of late-Victorian individualism. The designer, Sir Ernest George, was an English architect, but he was also a landscape and architectural watercolourist and an etcher. So the man behind these houses worked as an artist as well as a builder.
